LESSON: GENERAL ANIMAL HEALTH

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Animal Production
Topic 2.3: General Animal Health
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers General Animal Health, part of Animal Production in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How is animal health important in animal production? 2. How can we prevent animal diseases?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the benefits of keeping animals healthy in livestock production,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of General Animal Health in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compare signs of ill health and normal health in livestock production,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of General Animal Health in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. propose general control measures against ill Learner is guided in purposive groups, pairs or individually to: ● use information from digital and print resources to explain the benefits of keeping animals healthy in livestock production. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ write/ type or use Augmentative and Alternative modes of Communication, AAC to 1. How is animal health important in animal production? 2. How can we prevent animal diseases? 34 health in livestock production,

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. adopt practices that maintain animal health in livestock production. explain. Regulate glare on the digital devices screens for learners who are sensitive to light. Learners with postural difficulties could be appropriately positioned to enhance access to the devices, ● Observe animals in a herd and discuss with a resource person sign that show differences between sick and healthy livestock animals, ● suggest and discuss general preventive and control measures against ill health in livestock production, ● practise applicable measures that maintain animal health in livestock production and apply them in rearing available animals in school. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any alternative functional part of the body to carry out ability-level tasks. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on General Animal Health together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Patriotism: learner demonstrates moral duty in protecting animals against ill health by practising applicable measures of

animal disease control when rearing animals in the school.

● Respect: learner displays humility when discussing with a resource person the signs of ill health and good health in

livestock animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Health promotion issues: learner explains why keeping animals healthy can prevent zoonotic diseases which affect

humans.

● Animal welfare: learner observes animal welfare by practising applicable measures that maintain animal health.

Suggested Learning Resources: Video clips, photographs of ill animals in the immediate environment and in school with legible

print and clear colour contrast, Relevant materials and equipment such as antiseptics, drugs, bolus gun, hypodermic syringes and

needles, Adapted computers with appropriate accessibility features, Appropriate applications/ software, Ergonomic and head

operated mouse and footboards, Writing resources, Positioning devices, ICT tools with appropriate accessibility features, Other

related services (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, learner support)
